additionalTopics.title: 教学指导
additionalTopics.summary: Prior approval is required through the AI System for Assurance and Evaluation before deploying AI to provide instruction, feedback, or marks (Section 2.4). Instructors should be transparent about AI deployment (Section 2.1). In general, except for AI marking of objective or closed-ended assessments, a human instructor or reviewer should remain in the loop. Spot checks should still be conducted even where AI scoring is considered reliable.
additionalTopics.scope: Teaching staff, institutional services or disciplinary procedures as specified by the source; no extension to all student use.

claims.text: Policy for the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning (Current version 15 Sept 2026)

evidence.quote:
The use of AI tools to provide instruction to learners in the form of responses, feedback and/or
marks, whether as virtual tutors or as markers, requires prior approval by the Head of Department
or relevant Deanery, under the oversight of the Chair of the AI-COP. This is meant as due diligence
to balance innovation with ethical considerations. Institutional approval also shields the
individual instructors from complaints. Approval must be obtained through a submission to the
AI System for Assurance and Evaluation.
evidence.title: Policy for the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning (Current version 15 Sept 2026)

evidence.quote:
Instructors should be transparent about where and how they deploy AI in NUS courses. This is
especially important where AI is deployed to generate course content (including assessment
questions), to function as virtual tutors to answer student queries, or to help with assessment
feedback and grading.
evidence.title: Policy for the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning (Current version 15 Sept 2026)

evidence.quote:
In general, except for AI marking of objective or closed-ended assessments, a human instructor
or reviewer should always be in the loop, e.g., to review, revise, and finalize the output of the AI.
Failure to comply with this section may constitute a breach of University policy and may be
addressed through the relevant staff governance processes.
evidence.title: Policy for the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning (Current version 15 Sept 2026)

evidence.quote:
Even where there is
confidence that an AI tool can reliably generate accurate scores or comments without human
intervention, spot checks should still be conducted on the output. In all cases, the instructor
remains ultimately responsible for the use of the tool and its impact on learners (see 2.2 above).
evidence.title: Policy for the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning (Current version 15 Sept 2026)
